newsitem.title: USA: Unabomber trial set for November 1997.
newsitem.headline: Unabomber trial set for November 1997.

text.p: The trial of Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski on charges of killing two people with four bombs will begin in November next year, more than 18 months after his arrest, a federal judge ruled on Friday.

U.S. District Judge Garland Burrell ordered the trial to begin on November 12, 1997, after a 75-minute hearing in Sacramento at which prosecutors argued for an earlier start and defence attorneys sought more time to study the evidence.
Law enforcement officials believe Kaczynski is the shadowy Unabomber who killed three people and injured 23 during an anti-technology bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995.
The Sacramento trial will involve charges stemming from only four of the bombings and two of the killings. He has also been charged with a killing in New Jersey.

Kaczynski, 54, appeared in court for the first time on Friday since he was arraigned in Sacramento on June 25. He was wearing a brown tweed jacket, his hair and beard were neatly cropped, and he looked relaxed as he sat between his attorneys, chatting with them and smiling from time to time.
The prosecution, eager to get on with the case, had suggested a May 1997 trial date in court papers filed before Friday's hearing, but at the hearing, proposed a September 1997 start.

Defence attorneys argued against setting a trial date at this stage, suggesting the judge wait until next June instead so they would have a clearer idea of the amount of time needed for pre-trial motions.
Defence Attorney Quin Denvir appealed to the judge not to set the trial until November if he did feel it necessary to set a date.
"It's just a huge case. It's a monster case, like a huge antitrust case in terms of documents, information and investigative leads," Denvir said.
Defence attorneys said the prosecution has already turned over a vast amount of evidence to the defence and more still had to be turned over.

The Harvard-educated Kaczynski was arrested at his Montana cabin in April and transferred two months later to Sacramento where he was charged with four of the bombings, two of them deadly. He pleaded not guilty. The government has not said whether it will seek the death penalty.
Kaczynski has been indicted in New Jersey on charges he mailed a bomb that killed advertising executive Thomas Mosser in December 1994.
